intro_html: Etouffee means smothered, and that is exactly what happens here: chicken thighs buried in a roux-thickened Cajun gravy with the holy trinity of onion, celery, and bell pepper. Each bowl delivers a serious 50 grams of protein at 623 calories for about $2.03. The roux takes patience; everything else is a simmer.
cost_closing_html: About $2.03 a bowl for chicken etouffee that a New Orleans restaurant would price at seven or eight times that, and you did not have to find parking in the Quarter.
shop_smart: Seven pounds of boneless skinless chicken thighs is the backbone here, and the club pack price per pound is why this stays near two bucks a bowl.
The holy trinity of onion, celery, and bell pepper costs a couple dollars total. Buy whole heads and bunches, never the pre-chopped tubs at triple the price per ounce.
Flour and oil make the roux for pennies. Restaurants charge you for the 20 minutes of stirring; at home, that labor is free and you can listen to a podcast.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Make the roux: heat the vegetable oil in your largest heavy pot over medium, whisk in the flour, and stir near-constantly for 10 to 15 minutes until it turns the color of peanut butter. Do not walk away; a burnt roux starts over.
Add the butter, diced onion, celery, and green bell pepper and cook 5 to 6 minutes until softened. Add the garlic for 1 minute more.
Gradually whisk in the chicken broth so the roux stays smooth, then add the Worcestershire, Cajun seasoning, thyme, bay leaves, and hot sauce.
Add the chicken thighs, cut into large bite-size pieces, and bring to a gentle simmer.
Simmer uncovered 25 to 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until the gravy thickens and the chicken reaches 165F. Pull the bay leaves and stir in most of the green onions.
Meanwhile, cook 3.75 cups dry rice with water per package directions.
Combine the rice and etouffee in your weighed pot, or portion rice first and ladle the etouffee over, your call. Finish with the remaining green onions.
portion_html: Set the full pot on the scale, subtract the empty-pot weight, and divide by 14. Ladle that weight into each of 14 containers, gravy and all. Every bowl lands at 623 calories and 50 grams of protein.
upsell_html: Hearty dinners for about $2.03 a bowl. This is one of many. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons, calculators, and tools, all for $1 a month.

steps: Stir oil and flour over medium heat 10 to 15 minutes into a peanut-butter-colored roux.
Cook the onion, celery, and bell pepper in the roux with butter, then add garlic.
Whisk in the broth gradually, then season with Worcestershire, Cajun seasoning, thyme, and hot sauce.
Add the chicken and simmer 25 to 30 minutes until thickened and 165F.
Cook the rice, combine with the etouffee and green onions, and portion into 14 containers.
